item.title: Navy links operational successes to troops’ physical fitness
item.description: ….CNS urges personnel to sustain discipline, readiness By Kingsley Omonobi The Chief of the Naval Staff, Vice Admiral Idi Abass, has attributed operational successes recorded by the Nigerian Navy in 2026 against oil theft, maritime crimes and other security threats to the high physical standards and fitness of its personnel. Abass said the successes recorded in Operation Delta Sentinel and other joint operations across the country underscored the importance of physical fitness, endurance and teamwork among naval personnel. He spoke on Saturday while addressing officers and ratings during the Nigerian Navy’s Fourth Quarter Route March at the Naval Base, Abuja. He was represented by the Director of Project Implementation and Monitoring, Rear Admiral ML Dahiru. The naval chief said personnel had disrupted illegal refining sites, recovered suspected stolen crude oil and denied criminal elements proceeds from their activities. He added that naval personnel had also rescued kidnapped victims, protected critical maritime infrastructure, secured waterways and participated in ongoing counter-terrorism and counter-insurgency operations against violent extremist groups. “Our operational successes this year, particularly in Operation Delta Sentinel and across joint theatres nationwide, demonstrate why physical standards matter. “Behind each of these results are personnel who can sustain long hours on duty, remain alert as fatigue sets in and work together when the pressure is greatest,” he said. Abass explained that the quarterly route march was designed to build collective endurance, improve the physical fitness of personnel and strengthen teamwork across naval commands and formations. According to him, the exercise reinforces the standard that every officer and rating must remain physically fit and ready to respond whenever duty calls. He said the exercise also supported his mission to build a highly motivated and professional naval force capable of safeguarding Nigeria’s maritime interests and contributing effectively to joint military operations. The CNS noted that physically fit personnel were better equipped to meet the demands of patrols, emergency responses and joint counter-terrorism and counter-insurgency operations. Commending the dedication and resilience of the personnel, Abass urged them to sustain the discipline, vigilance and teamwork demonstrated during the exercise in their daily assignments. “As the year draws to a close, I urge you to carry the same discipline, vigilance and teamwork you demonstrated today into every assignment. While the Route March is quarterly, readiness is a daily responsibility,” he said. item.title: Apathy mars INEC mock accreditation exercise in Abia
item.description: …Voter alleges demand for N1m to participate By Steve Oko UMUAHIA — Voter apathy marred the mock accreditation and result-upload exercise conducted by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in Abia State on Saturday, with several polling units recording zero or minimal turnout. At Ibeku High School, one of the designated polling centres, Vanguard observed at about noon that no voter had turned up, while INEC officials waited for participants. A staff member of YIAGA Africa, who was monitoring the exercise, was also sighted at the centre but declined to comment. The situation was similar at School Road Primary School and Ugba Primary School, where electoral officials were on ground but voters were absent. Voters fault poor publicity, limited coverage At St. Stephen’s Primary School, Umuahia, however, some residents who turned out expressed disappointment that the exercise was restricted to selected polling units, blaming inadequate publicity for the low participation. Chimwe Kanu, a public servant, said she was excited about participating until she discovered that her polling unit was not among those selected for the exercise. “I’m happy to be here and to do the needful, but coming here, nothing is really happening because I was unable to vote or be captured. My polling unit is not part of the polling units selected. “I’m very disappointed because the happiness I came with, I didn’t see it again,” she said. Kanu said many prospective participants left after discovering that the exercise was limited to designated polling units. She urged INEC to improve its preparations for the 2027 general elections, particularly by ensuring the timely distribution of Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs). “Many don’t have their voters’ cards. Their names are here, but their voters’ cards have not been given to them. They should make sure they share the voters’ cards as soon as possible. People need their voters’ cards,” she said. She also called on the commission to ensure early arrival of election officials and seamless accreditation of eligible voters, expressing hope that it would conduct credible elections in 2027. Similarly, Mike Uche criticised the publicity for the exercise, saying many residents arrived at polling centres unaware that participation was restricted to designated units. He said inadequate sensitisation left many confused and frustrated, alleging that some prospective participants demanded financial inducements before agreeing to take part in the exercise. Uche urged INEC to intensify voter education through radio announcements, community outreach and street sensitisation to improve participation and enlighten the electorate on the purpose of such exercises. “People are eager to come out and do the mock accreditation. They didn’t give the proper publicity,” he said, adding that participation should not be reduced to financial demands. item.title: Low turnout mars INEC mock accreditation exercise in Katsina
item.description: By Fauziyya Lawal, Katsina Low voter turnout and inadequate public awareness characterised the mock accreditation exercise conducted by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in Katsina State on Saturday ahead of the 2027 general elections. Vanguard monitoring of the exercise at Star Election Polling Unit, Wakilin Kudu 1, Kofar Gidan Iro Isansi, Rafin Dadi, showed that only a few voters turned out to participate, although some were successfully accredited. The low participation raised concerns about the level of public sensitisation and awareness among eligible voters regarding the importance of the exercise. The mock accreditation exercise is designed to test the functionality of the accreditation system, assess the preparedness of electoral officials and identify possible technical and operational challenges ahead of the actual elections. At the polling unit, the participation of the few voters provided an opportunity to observe the practical application of the accreditation process and assess the readiness of electoral personnel. The development also highlighted the need for increased public enlightenment to ensure that eligible voters understand the purpose and significance of such exercises. Adequate sensitisation is considered essential to encouraging participation in mock exercises, which enable electoral authorities to test arrangements and address possible challenges before the main elections. The exercise also provides an opportunity to identify operational gaps and resolve potential difficulties that could affect the smooth conduct of the 2027 general elections. INEC is expected to strengthen public enlightenment and stakeholder engagement to improve awareness and encourage greater voter participation in subsequent electoral exercises. The post Low turnout mars INEC mock accreditation exercise in Katsina appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 2027: Low turnout mars INEC mock accreditation in Lagos
item.description: Voters blame poor publicity for low participation By Olayinka Ajayi Low turnout of eligible voters marred the mock accreditation exercise conducted by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) in parts of Lagos State on Saturday, with some voters blaming the commission’s inadequate publicity. Polling agents expressed concern over the poor participation when Vanguard visited some of the designated polling units in Ijegun, Satellite Town and Festac, in the Amuwo-Odofin area of the state. An INEC polling agent at one of the polling units said only about 40 of the 250 registered voters had participated in the exercise as of the time of the visit. “The turnout has not been encouraging here. So far, about 40 people had voted out of 250 registered voters, and the BVAS has been cooperating smoothly due to good network. So we are certain of uploading the results after the exercise,” the agent said. A chieftain of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) in Festac, Mr Olusegun Samuel, attributed the low turnout to inadequate awareness among residents. He alleged that many eligible voters were unaware that the mock accreditation exercise was taking place. “Apart from the ruling APC, many people are not even aware that mock accreditation took place today. “INEC is encouraging voter apathy by not engaging in active publicity. By this, the ruling party would still have its way come the 2027 general elections,” he said. However, a chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Saheed Bakare, described the exercise as encouraging, despite the challenges and low turnout. He said INEC officials arrived at the polling unit around 9 a.m. and met some voters waiting to participate. “So far, so good. The exercise is not perfect but encouraging. INEC polling agent came around 9 a.m. and met voters on ground waiting for them. “Although we noticed poor turnout, maybe because of poor publicity, but on our own side as a party, we tried to sensitise our people too,” he said. Bakare described the exercise as an opportunity to assess his party’s level of preparedness ahead of the 2027 general elections. item.title: Dangote Refinery set to list on NGX December 1
item.description: By Peter Egwuatu Dangote Petroleum Refinery & Petrochemicals FZE is scheduled to list 125,458,915,901 ordinary shares at N525 per share on the Main Board of Nigerian Exchange Limited (NGX) on Tuesday, 1 December 2026. The listing is expected to add approximately N65.87 trillion to the market capitalisation of NGX. The listing follows the company’s Initial Public Offering (IPO), which attracted approximately 3.8 million subscribers from 121 countries, including all 54 African countries, reflecting unprecedented investor participation in a Nigerian public equity offering. With a minimum subscription of N5,250 for 10 ordinary shares, the offer enabled investors across income groups and geographical locations to participate in the ownership of one of Africa’s largest industrial enterprises. Speaking at the launch of the IPO in September, Aliko Dangote, President and Chief Executive of Dangote Industries Limited, described the offer as an opportunity to broaden public ownership and enable more Nigerians and Africans to participate in industrial wealth creation. “The Dangote refinery IPO is more than an investment opportunity; it is an opportunity for millions of Nigerians and Africans to build lasting wealth through ownership of a world-class industrial asset,” Dangote said. Investor participation at this scale was facilitated by NGX Invest, the SEC-approved digital capital-raising platform launched by Nigerian Exchange Group Plc (NGX Group) in June 2024. By enabling a network of 186 distribution channels, including stockbrokers, banks, fintech platforms and WhatsApp, NGX Invest provided the rail that significantly broadened access to the public offer. Temi Popoola, Group Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of NGX Group, said: “The listing of Dangote Petroleum Refinery will mark an important milestone for Nigeria’s capital market, demonstrating its capacity to support large-scale industrial enterprises and mobilise long-term capital. The breadth of investor participation in the public offer also reflects the progress we have made in expanding market access. Through technology, strategic partnerships and a diverse distribution network, we are connecting more people to investment opportunities and more businesses to capital.” According to the company’s prospectus, net proceeds from the IPO will partly finance an estimated US$14.3 billion expansion programme designed to double refining capacity from 700,000 to approximately 1.4 million barrels per day. The transaction underscores the capital market’s strategic role in financing industrial expansion, broadening economic participation and supporting Nigeria’s ambition of becoming a US$1 trillion economy. Government officials, regulators, business leaders, market operators and representatives of African exchanges are expected to attend the listing ceremony. item.title: INEC, security agencies addressing security concerns ahead of 2027 polls – Amupitan
item.description: Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan, says the commission, in collaboration with security agencies, is taking necessary steps to address all security concerns ahead of the 2027 general elections. Amupitan ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍⁠​⁠‌‌‍‍‌‌​stated this on Saturday in Jos while speaking with newsmen during the monitoring of the ongoing mock accreditation. Addressing a question on the security challenge and the likely implications on voter participation, Amupitan said the safety of ad hoc staff and all Nigerians remained a priority to the commission. “As the chairman of INEC, I’m also worried about the state of security in Nigeria, but you can see we are taking some good steps to ensure that we nip it in the bud. “Just two days ago, we had a national security conference where we brought together all the members of the Inter-Agency Consultative Committee on Election Security (ICCES), the police, the military, the Civil Defence, and other paramilitary agencies. “So, we had a one-day conference where we discussed all these issues,” he said. Amupitan said that INEC had conducted a risk assessment of every part of Nigeria, using Election Risk Management (ERM) tools. “We have identified all the polling units that are vulnerable, and we have shared this with the law enforcement agencies so that they can make extraordinary preparation for those places. “Any polling unit 500 meters from those vulnerable areas has been identified, and we are going to deal with it,” he said. Amupitan said the commission was interested in the security of the voters and ad hoc staff, particularly corps members. “It’s not every security matter you can bring to the open, but we are doing everything, both intelligence and physical, to ensure that the security on election day is assured,” he said. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the monitoring of the mock accreditation exercise was still ongoing in different parts of the state as of the time of filling this report. (NAN) The post INEC, security agencies addressing security concerns ahead of 2027 polls – Amupitan appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Electricity’ll improve, Mbah and I are working on Eastern Gas Pipeline – Tinubu
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has said electricity supply will improve in the South-East, adding that his administration has approved the Eastern Gas Pipeline and Eastern Nigeria rail line as part of plans to boost infrastructure and connectivity in the region. Tinubu made the remarks on Saturday during the All Progressives Congress presidential campaign rally in Enugu, where he said he was working with Enugu State Governor Peter Mbah on the gas pipeline project. “Electricity will improve. The Eastern Gas Pipeline is approved. Peter Mbah and I are working on it,” the president said. He also announced the approval of the Eastern Nigeria rail line, saying the projects would improve connections between the South-East, South-South and northern parts of the country. “Also approved is the Eastern Nigeria rail line. We will connect you, connect the East, South and North. It’s our honest promise for development,” he said. Addressing farmers in the region, Tinubu promised interest-free loans and financial support, alongside measures to reduce the challenges associated with farming. “To our farmers, they will receive money, loans that are interest-free. We will relieve them of the burdens of farming. We will connect with infrastructure,” he said. The president also urged residents to participate in the January 16 election, asking them to collect their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) and turn out to vote for the APC. “January 16, you must go out and vote. Take your friends, take your brothers, take your sisters. You must collect your PVC and go there, for President, vote APC, for honourable, APC,” Tinubu said. item.title: Referee faces suspension after punching goalkeeper in post-match rawl
item.description: A Bolivian referee, Jordy Aleman, might face be faced with strict suspension rules after punching Real Potosi goalkeeper Cristian Martinez during a post-match confrontation following the 2026 Copa Bolivia final. The incident occurred on Wednesday after Always Ready secured the trophy with a 3-1 aggregate victory over Real Potosi. The second leg ended in a goalless draw at the Victor Agustin Ugarte Stadium in Potosi. Tensions flared after the final whistle as Real Potosi players approached Aleman to protest decisions made during the match. Television footage showed the referee punching Martinez in the face, triggering further disorder before police intervened to protect the officials. Reports from Spanish-language media, including MARCA, said the confrontation followed an insult directed at Aleman by the goalkeeper. Martinez reportedly told the referee, “I hope your mother dies.” Martinez later said the punch left his mouth bleeding. However, in a defiant response reported by El Diario, he remarked: “He should hit harder.” The goalkeeper also questioned Aleman’s professionalism and called for an exemplary punishment. He subsequently announced that he would not pursue legal action or file a formal complaint over the incident. In a statement shared by Spanish publication 20 Minutos, Martinez said: “My intention is to consider this episode over and avoid allowing this situation to continue generating conflict.” Aleman could face disciplinary sanctions under the Bolivian Football Federation’s Disciplinary Code, which reportedly provides for fines of at least 20 national minimum monthly salaries and bans of between one and three years for physical assaults. The incident also led to four Real Potosi players and three members of the club’s coaching staff reportedly receiving red cards. According to Bolivian publication Vision 360, the federation’s refereeing authorities are expected to review the incident alongside the match reports. Aleman’s status as an international referee could also have further implications. The referee has yet to make a public statement on the incident. The post Referee faces suspension after punching goalkeeper in post-match rawl appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Meet Nigerian’s Maria Wophill named World Athletics’ Woman of the Year
item.description: Veteran Nigerian sports administrator Maria Wophill has been named the World Athletics (WA) 2026 Woman of the Year in recognition of her decades-long contribution to gender equality and the development of women and girls in athletics. World Athletics announced the honour as part of its 2026 awards, recognising Wophill’s efforts to create opportunities for women in track and field through leadership, advocacy and grassroots development. Wophill previously served as secretary-general of the Athletics Federation of Nigeria (AFN) between 2005 and 2013. She has also held senior positions in the Federal Ministry of Youth and Sports Development and served on the World Athletics Women’s Committee from 2010 to 2018. Her contributions to Nigerian sports administration include advocacy for increased female representation on the boards of national sports federations, which helped secure additional positions for women. At the continental level, she championed the establishment of the Confederation of African Athletics (CAA) Gender Leadership Task Force in 2024. She has also mentored female coaches and sports administrators through the Women’s Sport Leadership Academy (WISH), while supporting grassroots participation through the Abuja FCT Girls Sprints and Relays, an initiative aimed at encouraging secondary school girls to take part in athletics. Reacting to the recognition, Wophill expressed gratitude to World Athletics and Nigerian sports organisations, describing the award as a motivation to continue contributing to the sport. “This has been a truly humbling year and I am very proud to be acknowledged for the work I have done,” she said. She added that the recognition had strengthened her commitment to promoting gender leadership, safeguarding young athletes and mentoring people within athletics. “This award has energised me to keep giving my best in all positions in athletics, with particular focus on gender leadership, safeguarding young athletes and mentoring within the sport,” she said. World Athletics President Sebastian Coe described Wophill as a deserving recipient, praising her efforts to improve female representation and mentor others in the sport. Her recognition is part of the 2026 World Athletics Awards, with the World Athletes of the Year, Rising Stars and Moment of the Year scheduled to be announced on Sunday. item.title: [PHOTOS] Moment Voter Makes Frustrating Facial Expressions While Being Captured On INEC’s BVAS
item.description: A voter at polling unit 001 in Barnawa, Kaduna South Local Government Area, captured attention on Saturday, as she made different frustrating facial expressions while being captured on the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) during the INEC’s mock accreditation exercise in Kaduna State. Our correspondent, who monitored the exercise, noted that a voter spent more than five minutes completing the accreditation and voting process due to network challenges affecting the machine. The exercise is expected to simulate the Presidential election, with polling units opening by 8:30 a.m. and accreditation running from 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. Meanwhile, one of the voters at polling unit 002, Narayi Primary School, in Kaduna State, Rebecca Oladipo, has expressed frustration over the absence of the Independent National Electoral Commission’s officials at the mock accreditation on Saturday. Oladipo, who said she arrived at the polling unit for the INEC mock accreditation exercise at 10:30 am, questioned the commission’s preparedness to conduct a credible election in 2027, expressing concern that the mock election, which is expected to test INEC’s operational readiness, appears to be starting on a shaky note. According to her, the delay left those who turned up for the exercise waiting without knowing when the exercise would commence. Rebecca Oladipo “I’m here at Narayi Primary School, one of the wards chosen for the mock exercise. I have been here for the past two hours. INEC is supposed to start the exercise at 8:30. Now we are at around 10:30, and we are yet to see them. “This is really disheartening because a lot of people have been here. Security agencies have been here; even I came to meet them here. One or two voters have been here, and they left. “I’m using this opportunity to say to INEC that we in Narayi ward are not happy because we heard that other wards have started the exercises, so we should not be left behind. “I’m using this opportunity to tell INEC that in the main election, please, please, let it not be like this. It has always been like this in the previous elections. Maybe because Narayi people are good and kind people. They are quiet people. “But please, I hope that everyone knows that the 2027 general election is a critical one. So, we are begging that they should make everything available. “Whatever may make them come late during the 2027 election, they should please avoid it.” The mock exercise, expected to simulate the Presidential election, is expected to open by 8:30 a.m., and accreditation will run from 8:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m. The post [PHOTOS] Moment Voter Makes Frustrating Facial Expressions While Being Captured On INEC’s BVAS appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Low turnout, BVAS glitches mar INEC mock accreditation in Ondo
item.description: By Dayo Johnson Akure The ongoing mock accreditation and voting exercise conducted by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) ahead of the 2027 general elections has recorded low voter turnout in some polling units in Ondo State, alongside technical challenges with the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS). As of the time of filing this report, findings showed that only two persons voted out of 470 registered voters at Tipper Garage, Ward 2, Unit 046. Similarly, at Champion Junction, Ward 3, Unit 15, only six voters participated in the exercise. At High Court, Ward 5, Unit 11, 11 persons were recorded as having voted out of 940 registered voters. However, the situation was different at Ajipowo, Ward 2, Unit 17, where a large turnout of voters was observed. Despite the turnout, the exercise experienced technical challenges as the BVAS reportedly failed to capture the faces of some elderly voters, causing difficulties during the accreditation process. The mock exercise is part of INEC’s preparations to test its electoral equipment and processes ahead of the 2027 general elections. item.title: Why Tinubu should stay in office for 10 years – Akande
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Former Osun State Governor, Bisi Akande, has called for President Bola Tinubu to remain in office for 10 years, saying the period would allow him to complete ongoing projects and deliver lasting reforms. Akande made the call during an interview on the Frankly Speaking with Icon podcast, published on Friday. “He should remain in office, if possible, for another 10 years; otherwise, we go back to the situation of ‘Ebinpawa’ because there has been a foundation for hunger,” Akande said. He cited the Olubadan’s comments on road projects across the South-West, including routes linking Ijebu-Ode, Abeokuta, Oyo and Ikire, as evidence of the administration’s ongoing work. Quoting the traditional ruler, Akande said: “If you are working like this, and this had not been done 50 years before you, what again do we still say you should do, and you have not done? “But so that you will be able to complete this good job that you started, Ibadan people and Oyo State people are supporting you to do another four years.” Akande also blamed successive military administrations for what he described as decades of neglect of agriculture, education and economic development, saying their policies contributed to the country’s present difficulties. “Forty years before he came, since 1966, when the military started ruling you, you have been laying the foundation for hunger. You have abandoned your farms. You have abandoned the job. You have refused to be educated. You have refused to be modernised,” he said. He expressed optimism that Tinubu’s policies would produce significant improvements in the coming years, particularly in electricity supply and modernisation. “So in another 10 years there will be electricity everywhere. There will be modernisation,” he said. “They liberalised electricity. If you have money today, you can create electricity in your home. You can create it in your city. You can create it around you,” he said. Comparing the policy with the restrictions under previous military administrations, Akande said individuals were previously prevented from generating electricity independently. “Unlike what the military did before, if you tried to create electricity, they would arrest you. They would make you a debtor. They wouldn’t let you do it. They said only the Federal Government could do it. Tinubu came and said everybody can do it,” he added. On his own public engagements, the former governor attributed his reduced movement around the country to age, contrasting his present situation with when he was younger. item.title: Low voter turnout mars INEC mock election in Bayelsa, as accreditation process runs smoothly
item.description: •Reports across the state indicate a seamless exercise despite poor participation By Samuel Oyadongha, Yenagoa The mock election organised by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) recorded a low voter turnout across Yenagoa, the Bayelsa State capital, on Saturday, despite reports of a smooth accreditation process. The exercise, designed to test the commission’s preparedness and assess the performance of its electoral technology ahead of the 2027 general elections, was seamless at the polling units visited. At the Kpansia Epie Community Town Hall, no fewer than nine voters had completed the accreditation process as of 11:15 a.m. when this reporter left the unit. The Assistant Presiding Officer, Sampson Wale, confirmed that operations with the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) were seamless. The story is not different at Epie II CPS Opolo II and others. The BVAS is being tested as part of efforts to identify and address possible challenges before the general elections. Though participation was relatively low, INEC officials expressed optimism that voter turnout would improve as the exercise progressed. Reports from other parts of the state also described the mock exercise as smooth. item.title: PHOTOS: Low Turnout as INEC begins Mock Election
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) commenced its mock elections in Borno State to test-run voting equipment and logistical readiness ahead of the 2027 general elections. However, the exercise recorded a low voter turnout in some polling units visited by our correspondent due to what many residents described as “a lack of awareness”. The exercise, designed to evaluate the deployment of election personnel and the functionality of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) across all 27 local government areas of the state, also faced a slow start in some polling units. Across Jere and Maiduguri Metropolitan Councils security personnel, including police officers and the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) and Road Safety Officials, were present early at some polling units, INEC officials arrived late. At the Bulama Jidda polling unit in Gomari Airport, voting commenced at 8:44 a.m. after officials arrived, slightly behind schedule. However, poll workers and voters at the station confirmed that the BVAS machines functioned efficiently. “There is actually a low turnout, but the use of BVAS is smooth. At some point, we are using it offline, but will upload it when we reach areas with a robust network,” one polling unit officer stated. Interviews with residents across various areas revealed that public awareness of the exercise was generally poor, with many locals unaware that the mock election was taking place. At the Gwange III polling unit, turnout was similarly low. Some prospective voters said they encountered some technical hitches during accreditation, reporting that the BVAS failed to capture their fingerprints and facial features. Speaking on condition of anonymity, an Ad-hoc staff, noted that affected individuals were not issued ballot papers. Instead, their details were compiled for INEC to review and resolve prior to the general elections. At the Government House polling unit (Unit 001, Maisandari Ward), where voter turnout was notably impressive, the process ran without hitches. Abacha Anas, the Electoral Officer for Operations for INEC in the Maiduguri Metropolitan Council, described the exercise as smooth and successful.

item.title: Gunmen kill 51-year-old man, two others in fresh Plateau attack
item.description: By Golok Nanmwa, Jos Gunmen have killed three persons in a fresh attack on Nkiedowro community in Teegbe District of Bassa Local Government Area of Plateau State, throwing residents into mourning. The attack, which occurred on Friday night, claimed the lives of three Irigwe natives, bringing to 20 the number of Irigwe people reportedly killed within the week, according to the National Publicity Secretary of the Irigwe Youth Movement, Joseph Chudu Yonkpa. Yonkpa, who confirmed the killings in a statement made available to newsmen on Saturday, said the attackers launched two separate ambushes on the community. “Yesterday night, Fulani militias launched two separate ambushes at Nkiedowro, Teegbe District, killing three Irigwe natives,” he said. He identified the victims as Ngudo Kura, 51; Hosea Ishaya, 26; and Naomi Izeh, 22. “This makes it a total of 20 Irigwe people killed this week in an unprovoked manner,” Yonkpa added. He expressed condolences to the families of the victims and the entire Irigwe community, praying for the repose of the souls of the deceased. Our correspondent reports that the latest killings occurred barely two days after 17 persons were given a mass burial following an attack on the Tafi Gana community, also in Bassa Local Government Area. The development has heightened concerns over the security situation in the area, with residents reportedly apprehensive about possible further attacks. The Irigwe Youth Movement urged residents to remain vigilant and avoid movements that could expose them to danger. “We call on our people to intensify vigilance, avoid late-night and isolated movements, and report suspicious movements to the relevant authorities,” Yonkpa said. The group also appealed to security agencies to strengthen surveillance and take necessary measures to protect communities in the area. Efforts to get the reaction of security operatives were unsuccessful as of the time of filing this report. The post Gunmen kill 51-year-old man, two others in fresh Plateau attack appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: INEC Declares Readiness For 2027, Expresses Satisfaction With Plateau Mock Election
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has declared its readiness for the 2027 general elections, assuring Nigerians that it is committed to conducting free, inclusive, credible and transparent polls. INEC Chairman, Professor Joash Amupitan, gave the assurance while monitoring Saturday’s mock election in Plateau State, where he expressed satisfaction with the turnout of voters and the conduct of the exercise. Amupitan said the mock election was designed to test the functionality of the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) and the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV), as well as assess the efficiency of the accreditation process ahead of the 2027 general elections. INEC Chairman Amupitan inspecting the exercise in Jos on Saturday, November 28, 2026. He commended voters for their orderly conduct, expressing delight at seeing an elderly woman turn out for the exercise and successfully undergo accreditation. “You can see yourself that the turnout is very good. What we are trying to test is actually the working of the machines, which are the BVAS and the IReV, and voters are being accredited. You can see how orderly it is going. From what we have seen, I am impressed,” he said. The INEC chairman acknowledged the support of the Plateau State Independent Electoral Commission in mobilising residents for the exercise but noted that the environmental sanitation exercise earlier scheduled for Saturday may have affected early participation, as some residents had indicated they would be unable to come out in time. On the commission’s preparedness for the 2027 elections, Amupitan said INEC was determined to deliver one of the best elections in the country’s history. “For the 2027 general elections, INEC is prepared, and I want to assure all Nigerians that we are going to have one of the best elections. We are determined that the 2027 election will be free, inclusive, credible and transparent,” he stated. Addressing concerns over the security situation in the country, the INEC chairman said the commission was working with relevant security agencies to ensure the protection of voters and electoral personnel during the forthcoming elections. He disclosed that INEC recently convened a one-day national security conference where stakeholders deliberated on security challenges and measures to safeguard the electoral process. INEC Chairman, Joash Amupitan, seen addressing staff and voters in Jos on Saturday, NOVEMBER 28, 2026. Amupitan further revealed that the commission had conducted a risk assessment of polling units across the country, with identified locations shared with law enforcement agencies to enable them to strengthen security arrangements ahead of the elections. “We have done what we call a risk assessment of all the polling units in Nigeria, and we have identified all the polling units and shared them with the law enforcement agencies so that they can make extra preparations ahead of the elections,” he said. item.title: Kaduna doctor joins APC, pledges support for Tinubu, Uba Sani
item.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo A Kaduna-based medical doctor and development professional, Dr Philip Ataga, has joined the All Progressives Congress (APC), pledging to mobilise support for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu and Kaduna State Governor, Senator Uba Sani, in the 2027 general elections. Ataga formally registered as a member of the party on November 22, 2026, at Narayi Ward in Chikun Local Government Area of Kaduna State. Speaking shortly after his registration, he urged professionals across various fields to embrace partisan politics and contribute their expertise to governance and national development. He said professionals could no longer afford to remain on the sidelines while criticising the political system, stressing the need for active participation in decision-making and policy formulation. “It is time for professionals to also join politics and contribute their quota towards changing some of the ills in society. We cannot continue to stay on the sidelines and expect things to change,” he said. Ataga, whose professional experience spans public policy, healthcare and community development, said his decision to join the APC was driven by his desire to contribute to governance, grassroots development and effective service delivery. He said his medical background would enable him to contribute to addressing challenges in the healthcare sector, particularly improving access to quality medical services and strengthening healthcare institutions. According to him, healthcare development requires practical interventions beyond policy pronouncements, adding that the welfare of healthcare workers and patients must remain a priority. The medical doctor also identified youth inclusion, public safety, economic empowerment and community development as critical areas requiring sustained government attention. Explaining his decision to join the APC, Ataga said he was attracted by what he described as the party’s commitment to progressive governance, inclusion and its development agenda. He pledged to participate actively in the party’s activities and grassroots mobilisation, particularly in support of Tinubu and Uba Sani ahead of the 2027 elections. He maintained that professionals had important roles to play in strengthening public institutions, influencing policies and promoting sustainable development through active political participation. His entry into the APC comes amid increasing political activities ahead of the 2027 general elections, as political parties seek to attract professionals, technocrats and other stakeholders. item.title: Numbers ‘Impressive’ As Voters Turnout For INEC Mock Exercise In Kano
item.description: The mock accreditation for the 2027 general elections is underway in Paniso ward, Kano, as voters were seen turning out in seemingly impressive numbers for the exercise, compared to other regions in the country. Our correspondent, who monitored one of the selected polling units, noted that two INEC staff and two ad hoc personnel are testing the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) devices. Although voter turnout is still relatively low as against what is expected, the exercise is progressing smoothly, with no discrepancies reported and the BVAS thumbprint verification functioning as expected so far. Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Joash Amupitan, is currently in Jos to inspect the ongoing mock accreditation exercise, ahead of the 2027 general elections. It’s about seven weeks before the 2027 general election, and INEC is today running a nationwide mock accreditation and result transmission exercise in all 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). Professor Joash Amupitan, INEC Chairman, disclosed this at the INEC and Office of the National Security Adviser ONSA) Strategic Election Security Conference in Abuja on Thursday. According to him, the exercise would put the Commission’s new equipment and result systems under live conditions. “While this exercise allows INEC to stress-test our upgraded BVAS devices and verify our stricter INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV) validation safeguards—which automatically block arithmetic inconsistencies and over-voting, it also serves as an essential live dry run for our security architecture,” he said. The presidential and National Assembly elections hold on 16 January 2027 across 177,299 polling units, with governorship and State Houses of Assembly elections to follow on 6 February 2027. item.title: CHINA DIARIES: Where Students Build the Future
item.description: I must confess, I was not quite prepared for what I saw during my visit to the Qinling Workshop at Xi’an Aeronautical Vocational and Technical College in China. For someone fascinated by technology and innovation, walking into the institution’s aircraft hangar was an experience in itself. There were aircraft and helicopters, aviation equipment and specialised training facilities. For a moment, it felt less like visiting a school and more like stepping into an aviation engineering centre. But the biggest surprise was yet to come. Beyond the aircraft and helicopters, I encountered something that left an even stronger impression: drones designed, developed and assembled by students. China Diaries: The Railway Connecting Continents China Diaries: The future of farming These were not simply classroom models or academic projects put together to earn grades. The students were experimenting with different drone technologies, exploring their applications and developing solutions to practical problems. There were different designs and innovations, reflecting the creativity, technical confidence and curiosity of young people who were not waiting until graduation to start making a contribution to society. It was exciting to see. One could immediately imagine the possibilities: drones that could help farmers monitor crops and spray farmlands, support environmental monitoring, conduct aerial surveys, inspect infrastructure and assist emergency response operations. What struck me most was the philosophy behind what I was seeing. Technology was not being taught as an abstract subject. Students were being encouraged to understand problems and develop technological solutions. An institution built around practical skills The Qinling Workshop visit offered an opportunity to appreciate the work of Xi’an Aeronautical Vocational and Technical College, an institution with a strong focus on aviation, engineering and technical education. Its programmes cover a wide range of disciplines, including aviation manufacturing, aircraft maintenance, aircraft engine technology, drone application technology, general aviation, mechanical engineering, artificial intelligence, computer technology, robotics, automation, electronic information, aviation logistics and automotive technology. Students also study specialised areas such as CNC machining, intelligent manufacturing, aircraft electronic systems, materials engineering, welding technology, surveying and remote sensing, software development, big data, airport operations and civil aviation services. The breadth of these programmes is significant. It shows an understanding that an aviation and manufacturing economy requires much more than pilots and aircraft engineers. It needs technicians, software developers, mechanics, materials specialists, electronics experts, maintenance professionals and people who can design, manufacture and repair equipment.
